title: Thy first charity (Apocalypse 2:1–7)
hook: Ephesus works hard but has left its first love

segments.voice: Yesterday, alpha and omega carved into the Easter candle. Your line was the first and the last. Did you trace the two letters at a beginning and an end? Day six hundred twenty-one.

They run their home like a well-managed company. A shared calendar. The bills paid on time. The kids at practice, the groceries ordered, the car serviced. Nothing is falling apart. Ask either of them and they'd say things are fine. And they are fine. It's just that neither can remember the last time they sat on the porch and simply talked, the way they did when they first met, for hours, about nothing. After the vision of chapter one, the Apocalypse turns to seven short letters for seven churches. The first goes to the biggest city on the list, Ephesus. It's a letter to a very well-run church.
screen: `A HOME RUN LIKE A COMPANY.` → `NOTHING FALLING APART.` → `A LETTER TO EPHESUS.`

segments.voice: Ephesus was a great port city, home to a famous temple of the goddess Artemis. Paul had spent years there. Christian tradition says John lived there too, and some traditions add Mary. This was a church with history. And the letter opens with praise. I know your works, Christ says. Your labor, your patience. You can't stand evil. You've tested people who called themselves apostles and found them false. You've endured, for my name, and haven't grown weary. Then the turn. In the Douay-Rheims: "But I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity." First charity: your first love. Everything is working except the thing everything was for. The works are there. The love that started them has drifted away, the way a couple can keep a house running and stop really seeing each other. The remedy comes in three steps. Remember where you fell from. Repent, which the Douay-Rheims calls doing penance. And do the first works, the things you did when the love was new. Not new strategies. The first things. The warning is serious: otherwise, he says, I will move your candlestick out of its place. A church can stay busy and still go out like a lamp. But the letter ends with a promise, as every one of the seven does: to him that overcometh, I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of my God. The tree from the garden of Eden, closed off since Genesis, opens again at the end of the Bible.
screen: `EPHESUS: A CHURCH WITH HISTORY.` · `I KNOW THY WORKS.` · `THOU HAST LEFT THY FIRST CHARITY.` · `REMEMBER, REPENT, DO THE FIRST WORKS.` · then, large: `THE TREE OF LIFE, OPEN AGAIN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember your first love for God. Sit comfortably and breathe. Go back, as far as you need to, to a time when faith felt alive to you: a first Communion, a retreat, a moment in an empty church, a prayer that was answered, or simply a time you felt close to God. If you've never had a moment like that, think of the first time anything stirred your sense of wonder: a night sky, a piece of music. Let the memory come back in detail. What did you do then that you've stopped doing? If you pray, you can ask for that first love back. The bell holds the time.
Thy first charity. Apocalypse two: Ephesus kept working but left its first love, and is told to remember and do the first works. Today's word.
Your line: the first charity. Today, do one of the first works again, the thing you did when the love was new. Day six hundred twenty-one.

howItsDone: Catholics often return to their first love for God through retreats, renewing baptismal promises at Easter, going back to confession, or revisiting the prayers and practices that first drew them into faith.

fork.setup: you're a leader in the church at Ephesus. you work hard, you test false teachers, you haven't grown weary. the letter says you've left your first love. what are you told to do?
options: remember, repent, and do the first works.
fork.reveal: not more effort, not a new plan: go back. remember where you fell from, and do the first works, the things you did when the love was new.

original.note: Greek: thy first love (Apocalypse 2:4); the Douay-Rheims, following Latin caritas, says charity.

trapdoor: what you thought: a scolding for a church that stopped trying.
what it means: a busy, faithful church that kept working but lost the love that started it, told to go back to the first works.
what a scholar hears: prōtē can mean both earliest and foremost; every one of the seven letters shares a pattern: I know thy works, a call, a promise to the one who overcomes.

sources.quoted: But I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity.

notes: The promise in 2:7 is quoted without quotation marks in the voice ('to him that overcometh, I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of my God'), following the Douay-Rheims wording; confirm and consider adding as a quoted source.
Traditions that John lived at Ephesus (Irenaeus) and that Mary lived there with him (later tradition, e.g. the House of the Virgin Mary near Ephesus): framed as tradition. Confirm.
Paul in Ephesus 'for years': Acts 19:10 (two years) and Acts 20:31 (three years). Confirm phrasing.
Ephesus as 'the biggest city on the list' among the seven: confirm.
'Every one of the seven letters ends with a promise to the one who overcomes': confirm the pattern (2:7, 11, 17, 26; 3:5, 12, 21).
